title.narrative: Strengthening water science, innovation, education and management in Ecuador

description.narrative: Ecuador, as part of the Andean region, is characterized by an exceptional diversity of ecosystems across its four geographical regions: the Andes, the Amazon, the Coast, and the Galápagos Islands. The country is also home to numerous Indigenous Peoples and local communities, particularly in the highlands and the Amazon, whose ancestral knowledge and practices constitute valuable contributions to sustainable water management, climate change adaptation, disaster risk reduction, and environmental conservation. Recognizing the importance of integrating scientific knowledge with local and ancestral perspectives, UNESCO Quito will promote initiatives that strengthen the inclusion of Indigenous and local knowledge systems in water governance and management processes. Special attention will be given to engaging youth and Indigenous communities through research, capacity-building activities, and community-based projects linked to UNESCO-designated sites, including Biosphere Reserves, Geoparks and other recognized territories. Water-related challenges remain a priority political, institutional, environmental, and cultural issue in Ecuador. Through the framework of the Intergovernmental Hydrological Programme (IHP), UNESCO Quito has supported national efforts to strengthen water education, youth engagement, ecohydrology, and community participation, particularly through the consolidation of the Youth Water Network of Ecuador (Red Agua Ecuador), the organization of national youth encounters, capacity-building initiatives, and the promotion of Ecohydrology Demonstration Sites. Building on these achievements, during the 2026–2027 biennium UNESCO Quito will support the strengthening of water governance and scientific cooperation in Ecuador by facilitating the establishment and active operation of a National Committee of the Intergovernmental Hydrological Programme (CONAPHI), as well as the reactivation and engagement of Ecuadorian experts in IHP working groups and regional thematic networks. The Office will also promote innovation, knowledge exchange, and collaborative learning through water education initiatives, ecohydrology demonstration sites, citizen science activities, and youth-led actions. At the regional level, UNESCO Quito will foster dialogue, collective reflection, and the exchange of experiences among Andean countries on water education, ecohydrology, youth engagement, and integrated water resources management. These efforts will contribute to strengthening capacities, enhancing regional cooperation, and advancing sustainable and inclusive water governance across the Andean region.
